name: Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah International Airport
before:
Known to most people as Subang, this is the airport that served Kuala Lumpur from 1965 until 1998, when the much larger Kuala Lumpur International Airport at Sepang took over the long-haul traffic. It did not close. Instead it settled into a second life as Subang SkyPark, a smaller terminal in Selangor's Petaling District handling regional and domestic flights, charter work and a good deal of general aviation.

The draw is simple: it sits in the Klang Valley, much closer to central Kuala Lumpur than Sepang, so travellers heading into the city save themselves a long transfer. Batik Air Malaysia, Firefly, Berjaya Air, MHS Aviation and Weststar Aviation all operate from here, and commercial jet services returned in 2024, adding more regional routes to the board.

Expect a modest, workmanlike terminal rather than a sprawling international hub, which is part of its appeal for anyone who dislikes long walks between gates. The airport is also building up its aircraft maintenance and aerospace work, so clients may notice hangars and engineering activity alongside the passenger side of things.
after:
Known to most people as Subang, this is the airport that served Kuala Lumpur from 1965 until 1998, when the new Kuala Lumpur International Airport at Sepang took over. It did not close. Instead it settled into a second life as Subang SkyPark, a smaller airport in Selangor with domestic and regional flights.

The draw is simple: it is much closer to central Kuala Lumpur than Sepang, so travellers heading into the city save themselves a long transfer. Commercial jet flights returned in August 2024 after 22 years, and Batik Air is among the airlines flying from here.

Expect a modest, workmanlike terminal rather than a sprawling international hub, which is part of its appeal for anyone who dislikes long walks between gates.

claims.note: Was 'when the much larger Kuala Lumpur International Airport at Sepang took over the long-haul traffic'. The 1998 article dates Subang's opening to 30 August 1965 and says it was succeeded by the new airport at Sepang, opened by the King the Saturday before 30 June 1998; Wikipedia gives 1965 to 1998. 'Long-haul traffic' understates it: the new airport took over Subang's role as the main airport.

claims.note: Was 'a smaller terminal in Selangor's Petaling District handling regional and domestic flights, charter work and a good deal of general aviation'. The SkyPark terminal's own site and Wikipedia give the Subang SkyPark name; GeoNames puts Subang in Selangor; the ministry's tables show both domestic and international passengers (1,347,082 domestic and 506,487 international across 2025), and The Star (2024) describes its jet flights as regional. 'Smaller' is against Kuala Lumpur International Airport: in the fourth quarter of 2025 the ministry counts 479,247 passengers at Subang against 9,781,476 at KLIA and 7,159,338 at KLIA2. The district and the charter and general aviation work rest on Wikipedia alone.
